questions.stem: When must the operator of a pleasure craft keep a proper lookout?
options: Only at night or in fog
questions.explanation: The lookout duty applies at all times, by sight, hearing and any other means you have.

questions.stem: A boat off your port bow is getting closer. Its compass bearing stays the same. What does this tell you?
options: It will pass well ahead of you
There is a risk of collision
It is going the same speed as you
It will pass well astern of you
questions.explanation: A steady bearing with a closing distance means you are on a collision course. Act early.

questions.stem: Two power-driven boats are meeting nearly bow to bow. What should each one do?
options: Turn to starboard and pass port to port
Turn to port and pass starboard to starboard
Stop engines and wait for the other
Keep course and speed and sound one blast
questions.explanation: In a head-on situation both boats turn to starboard. Neither one is the stand-on boat.

questions.stem: You are in a powerboat. Another powerboat is crossing from your right side. What is your role?
options: Both boats must turn to port
questions.explanation: The boat that has the other on her starboard side gives way. Pass astern of her.

questions.stem: From where must a boat be coming up to count as overtaking another boat?
options: Anywhere forward of her beam on either side
Exactly abeam of her, on her port side
Within 10 degrees of right ahead of her
More than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam
questions.explanation: Overtaking means coming up from more than 22.5 degrees abaft the beam. The overtaking boat keeps clear.

questions.stem: Your powerboat is overtaking a slow sailboat that is under sail. Who must keep clear?
options: The sailboat, because it is slower
questions.explanation: An overtaking boat keeps clear, and a power-driven boat also keeps clear of a sailing vessel.

questions.stem: A power-driven pleasure craft must keep out of the way of which of these?
options: A seiner with her net out
questions.explanation: A vessel engaged in fishing with gear that limits her manoeuvring is higher in the order. Trolling lines do not count, and a sailboat under engine is a power-driven boat.

questions.stem: Two sailboats under sail are on a collision course. Boat A has the wind on her port side. Boat B has it on her starboard side. Who gives way?
questions.explanation: With the wind on different sides, the boat with the wind on her port side gives way.

questions.stem: Your 7 m boat is in a narrow channel. A ferry is coming that can only use the channel. What must you do?
options: Keep to starboard and do not impede her
Hold your course; she must steer round you
Cross ahead of her quickly to the far side
Stop in mid-channel and sound five blasts
questions.explanation: A boat under 20 m must not impede a vessel that can navigate only inside a narrow channel. Keep to the starboard side.

questions.stem: About how long does a prolonged blast last?
questions.explanation: A prolonged blast lasts 4 to 6 seconds. A short blast lasts about 1 second.

questions.stem: A tug in sight of you sounds two short blasts. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Two short blasts mean turning to port. One short is starboard, three short is astern.

questions.stem: A ship sounds five or more short, rapid blasts at your small boat. What is she telling you?
options: She is about to anchor here
She is leaving the dock now
questions.explanation: Five or more short blasts is the doubt and danger signal. Make your action clear and get out of her way.

questions.stem: In fog, a power-driven boat moving through the water sounds which signal?
options: One prolonged, at least every 2 minutes
Two prolonged, at least every 2 minutes
One short blast, at least every 30 seconds
Five short, at least every 2 minutes
questions.explanation: Making way: one prolonged blast at intervals of not more than 2 minutes. Two prolonged is for a power-driven boat that is stopped.

questions.stem: Which of these meets the rule for a sound-signalling device on a small pleasure craft?
options: A whistle with a pea inside
questions.explanation: A sound-signalling device is a pealess whistle or a compressed-gas or electric horn.
